newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Red Cross pulls out of "chaotic" east Zaire town.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross pulls out of "chaotic" east Zaire town.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) on Monday evacuated its two remaining expatriate staff members in the eastern Zairean town of Bukavu after security deteriorated sharply, a spokesman said.
The Geneva-based ICRC was among few relief agencies to stay behind in Bukavu after the United Nations evacuated some 100 expatriate employees at the weekend on orders from New York.
Ethnic Banyamulenge Tutsi rebels have advanced close to Bukavu. Zairean troops have looted aid agency vehicles and robbed foreigners and Zairean civilians in the lakeside city, aid workers said.
Aid agencies have already pulled out of the town of Uvira further south.
ICRC spokesman Rolin Wavre said in Geneva that the situation in Bukavu on Monday was one of complete chaos and insecurity.
"There's looting and drinking and no authority left anymore. People with arms are getting out of control. We had six vehicles stolen. There is complete insecurity and confusion," he said.

Following the evacuation of humanitarian staff, Wavre said it would be impossible to know what would happen to tens of thousands of Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees fleeing their camps in the region because of the fighting.
"People are scattered in the hills. They won't be helped at all," he said. "No one will be able to bring them anything."
